A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EMPALC study. The complete text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C are readable and matchable; the additional page in v2 reflects end-matter reflow.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original questionnaire assessments across 88 models and intervention experiments on seven models, including numerical results in Tables 2-3.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the original 88-model assessments and seven-model intervention results, including Tables 2-3.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same questionnaire-to-NLI prompt construction, MNLI fine-tuning, two-way normalization, scoring, and domain-adaptation procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use MNLI, the GAD-7, PHQ-9 and SoC-13 questionnaires, and the same depressive-mood, high-SoC and hate-speech adaptation corpora. No task or data coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: No comparator is added or removed. Figure 2 retains the raw-versus-normalized score comparison, and Table 3 retains the same original-versus-adapted model comparisons.

E3.justification: The 88-model selection, 1,408 prompts, validation metrics, corpus sample sizes, and seven-model intervention protocol are unchanged. Both report 20 adaptation epochs, learning rate 2e-5 and batch size 8.

E4.justification: The prompt-validity and consistency analyses, cross-construct correlations, hate-speech sentiment control, and BlenderBot response example in Sections 4.2-4.4 are retained without added or removed analyses.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains the same mean and standard-deviation reporting and paired t-tests. Variability and correlation-significance reporting in Section 4 is unchanged, with no new seed or repeated-run information.

E6.justification: Tables 1-3, Figures 2-3 and the results text retain the same numerical and qualitative findings, including the GAD-7/PHQ-9 correlation of r = 0.765 and the intervention outcomes. The appendices add no results.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of construct terms, intensifiers, normalization and weighted questionnaire scoring in Sections 3.1-3.2 are unchanged. No theorem, proof or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same claims about assessing conversational and non-conversational models through questionnaire-derived NLI prompts and identifying and manipulating human-like psychological constructs.

C2.justification: Section 5 retains the same interpretations of SoC interventions and MNLI fine-tuning biases, together with limitations concerning knowledge questionnaires, unnoticed biases and manual prompt design. Appendix B retains the same explanatory examples.

D1.justification: Hardware, training hyperparameters, corpus preparation details and model-selection instructions are unchanged. Section 5.1 retains the same code/data access statement and Creative Commons licensing information.

R1.justification: No cited work or research positioning is added or removed. Changes such as HLEG's publication year, the Gliem conference details and the Hutto-Gilbert DOI update metadata for existing references.

P1.justification: v2 adds an Acknowledgments paragraph identifying funding support and makes limited bibliographic and corresponding citation edits. The scientific narrative and existing section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-3 and Tables 1-3 are unchanged. The acknowledgment moves the References opening from page 9 to page 10; end-matter reflow and slightly increased acronym spacing leave three acronyms on an otherwise nearly empty page 13.

improvement.justification: v2 adds explicit funder and proposal disclosure and fuller publication details for existing references, modestly improving transparency and source traceability. Scientific evidence and limitations remain unchanged. The acronym list spilling onto a nearly empty final page is a small layout drawback.
